title: Profiles vs permission sets in source control and deployment
objectives: Explain why profile metadata is a poor default unit in Git compared with permission sets.
State that unlocked/2GP package version create keeps only profile settings related to the packaged metadata.
Choose permission sets (and groups) as the source-driven authorization deploy unit.
Separate assigning users (data-like operation) from deploying permission-set metadata.
diagnostic_question: A PR deploys the entire Admin profile XML to grant LAB_ object access, and an unlocked package version 'includes the profile.' What will reviewers and the package build actually keep?
definition: Profiles and permission sets are both authorization metadata, but they behave differently in source control and packaging. Profile XML is large, noisy to merge, and is trimmed at unlocked or 2GP version create to settings related to the package's metadata. Permission sets are additive collections of permissions that retrieve and deploy as focused metadata and are the usual source-driven way to grant LAB_ access. User assignments are not the same as deploying the permission-set definition. ([How We Handle Profile Settings in Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm); [Permission Sets](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.perm_sets_overview.htm); [Project Setup](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_workspace_setup.htm))
why_it_matters: Teams that commit Admin.profile-meta.xml fight Git, surprise package installs, and overwrite unrelated production permissions. Interviewers want permission sets in source, profiles as a thin baseline, and package profile trimming.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of hotel keys. A profile is the floor's default wiring: huge, shared, painful to rewire in Git. A permission set is a stackable key card for LAB_ doors only. Deploying the card is metadata; handing cards to guests is assignment. When you ship a package, the factory keeps only the wiring snippets that belong to the packaged rooms and throws the rest of the floor plan away.
deeper_explanation: Permission sets grant additional permissions to users on top of their profile. They are the documented way to extend access without cloning profiles for every job. Permission set groups bundle them. In a DX project they retrieve as small XML files that reviewers can read. ([Permission Sets](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.perm_sets_overview.htm))

Profiles remain in the platform as a baseline (login hours, some settings permission sets do not replace—Needs verification of the current 'profiles versus permission sets' Help table before listing every gap). As Git artifacts they are famous for merge conflicts because they include object, field, user, and app settings in one giant file (DEVOPS-003).

During unlocked or 2GP package version creation, the build inspects all profiles in the DX project and preserves only settings directly related to the package metadata. The profile itself and unrelated settings are discarded from the package. Do not expect Admin.profile in Git to become Admin in the subscriber org. ([Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm))

Deploying a permission set does not assign it to users. Assignments can be metadata in some retrieve shapes (PermissionSetAssignment is data-like / user-related—treat user assignment as a separate, careful operation; Needs verification of whether you retrieve assignments as metadata in your API version). Scratch-org docs tell you to assign a permission set after deploying source so users can see custom objects. Never grant via retrieving production User records into Git.

mental_model.analogy: Hotel keys: profile = default floor wiring (huge Git file); permission set = stackable key card for specific doors; package version create = factory that keeps only wiring for packaged rooms and discards the rest; assignment = handing cards to guests, not printing the card.
useful_mapping: profile XML in Git → rewiring the whole floor in one PR
permission set XML → one stackable card
permission set group → a ring of cards
package profile trimming → factory discards unrelated wiring
user assignment → handing the card over
Minimum Access / baseline profile → thin wiring you rarely diff
Admin profile retrieve → noisy merge and overwrite risk
scratch org after deploy → still need to assign the card
where_it_breaks: Some settings still live only on profiles; confirm current Help before saying permission sets do everything.
Managed package manageability can lock subscriber edits.
Assignment is not always 'data' in the DEVOPS-001 Account sense; still do not commit production users.
The hotel does not encode OWD or sharing rules (SEC track).

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Put permission sets in Git for feature access. Profiles are noisy and get trimmed in unlocked/2GP versions to related settings only. Deploying a permission set does not assign users. Do not ship Admin.profile as the authorization strategy.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I retrieve a small LAB_ permission set, review it in a PR, deploy it, then assign it in the scratch org. I keep a thin baseline profile I rarely touch. I explain package profile trimming so nobody expects Admin to clone. I keep OWD/sharing on the SEC track. I never commit production users to grant access.

interview_questions.question: Profiles versus permission sets in source control?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Permission sets are small additive metadata and the right Git unit for feature access. Profiles are huge, merge-hostile, and get trimmed in package versions.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I retrieve PermissionSet:LAB_… not Admin. I keep a thin baseline profile. I explain unlocked/2GP profile handling. I assign after deploy. I do not collapse sharing into this answer.
interview_questions.example: PR adds LAB_Boarding_User with LAB_Gate__c CRUD instead of 4,000 profile lines.
tradeoffs: One profile per job vs permission set explosion

interview_questions.question: What happens to profiles in an unlocked package version?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The build keeps only profile settings related to the package metadata and discards unrelated settings and the profile as a whole from the package.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I put permission sets in the package directory. I treat leftover profile files as a trap. I still may need subscriber-side assignment. I do not call this a platform bug.
interview_questions.example: Admin.profile in Git; install org Admin unchanged; LAB_ permission set present if it was packaged.
tradeoffs: Packaging permission sets vs unpackaged profile deploys
weak_answer_warnings: The whole Admin profile always ships

interview_questions.question: Scratch org has the object; the demo user cannot see it. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check the permission set contents and whether it was assigned. Deploy does not assign. Tab visibility and license also matter.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I run sf org assign permset. I inspect objectPermissions and tabSettings. I do not redeploy CustomObject in a loop. I do not retrieve production Users. I mention OWD only as a neighbor if records exist but list views are empty.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Boarding_User not assigned to the scratch user after project deploy start.
tradeoffs: Permset vs profile on the scratch user
follow_ups: How do you assign in CI?
weak_answer_warnings: The retrieve failed because the tab is missing from Git always

interview_questions.question: A teammate wants to deploy Admin.profile to production to 'sync permissions.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Refuse as a default. It overwrites unrelated production settings and is a merge nightmare. Ship permission sets for the feature delta.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show the diff size. I explain packaging trimming if they also package. I offer a permission set plus assignment list. If a genuine profile-only setting must move, I isolate that setting—Needs verification of current profile-only list—not the whole Admin file.
interview_questions.example: Replace a 5,000-line profile deploy with a 40-line permission set plus named assignees.
tradeoffs: Speed of one profile deploy vs blast radius
weak_answer_warnings: Production Admin should match Git Admin always

interview_questions.question: Design source-driven authorization for a 12-person app team.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Thin baseline profiles, permission sets per capability, groups per job, Git review, deploy, then assignment via a controlled process—not User records in the repo.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map capabilities to sets so PRs stay small. I use groups so assignment is one ring of cards. I keep CI assigning only scratch users. Production assignment may be an admin task or a governed tool. I document profile trimming for the unlocked package.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Boarding_User + LAB_Baggage_User in LAB_Agent_Group, baseline Minimum Access-style profile.
tradeoffs: Many small sets vs few fat sets

interview_questions.question: Is a permission set business data?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. It is authorization metadata you retrieve and deploy. User records are not the thing you version to grant it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: DEVOPS-001 still applies: the definition is metadata. Assignments attach to users. I will not Data Load the permission set XML. I will not Metadata API the Account rows to 'give access.'
interview_questions.example: LAB_Boarding_User.permissionset-meta.xml in force-app; three sandbox users assigned in Setup.
tradeoffs: Assignment as metadata vs as a post-deploy script
CMDT vs permission sets for flags
weak_answer_warnings: Permission sets are like Account teams data

interview_questions.question: Permission set is in Git and the org, user still denied a field.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check fieldPermissions in the XML, assignment, FLS versus object CRUD, then sharing/OWD as a neighbor, then license.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I retrieve the org copy to see drift. I do not widen to Admin.profile. I check if a permission set group mutes the field. I keep this troubleshooting on authorization metadata, not on deploy flags.
interview_questions.example: objectPermissions allowRead true but fieldPermissions for LAB_GateNumber__c missing.
tradeoffs: Fix the set vs add another set
follow_ups: How do you test as the user?

interview_questions.question: A Java security lead says 'put roles in Spring Security config.' Translate.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Our config is permission-set XML in Git, reviewed like code, deployed as metadata, assigned to users. Profiles are a bulky baseline, not the feature ACL file.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map Spring roles to permission sets, not to Salesforce Roles (that's hierarchy/sharing). I mention package trimming like a build that strips unused ACL lines. I mention assignment as a separate provision step. I do not claim OWD is Spring Security.
interview_questions.example: ROLE_BOARDING_AGENT → LAB_Boarding_User permission set in the DX project.
tradeoffs: Many fine-grained sets vs coarse roles
